<p style="font-size:14px;">
The American Redstart (*Setophaga ruticilla*) is a migratory songbird associated with young to mature deciduous and mixedwood forests, particularly habitats with dense understory vegetation and structurally diverse foliage. The species often occupies forest edges, regenerating stands, riparian woodlands, and areas with abundant shrub cover where it forages on insects and other arthropods. In the boreal region, habitat conditions are influenced by forest age, vegetation complexity, and disturbance patterns that shape the availability of suitable breeding habitat. Although American Redstart can use a range of forest conditions, changes in forest structure, loss of understory vegetation, and shifts in landscape composition may affect habitat suitability. This vulnerability assessment evaluates potential exposure to landscape changes and assesses factors that may influence habitat conditions for American Redstart within the assessment area.
</p>
